results.market_title: Will the highest recorded wind on Mt. Washington in October be at least 110 mph?
results.reasoning: Mt. Washington's summit is one of the windiest places on Earth, with October's all-time record gust at 161 mph (1943) and average October wind speed of 35.5 mph. Hurricane-force winds (74+ mph) occur regularly outside peak winter months, and the mountain's exposure to westerly flow funneling plus frequent fall frontal passages/nor'easters make gusts of 110+ mph common in most Octobers, though not guaranteed every single year. Lacking granular recent-year F6 data due to search limitations, I lean toward a high but not certain probability, roughly consistent with strong historical base rates for this threshold.

results.reasoning: Prediction market aggregators (Kalshi/Polymarket, via DeFiRate as of early Oct 2026) show the Oct 28, 2026 FOMC meeting pricing a hold as the clear favorite (~84%), with a hike around 17-18% and a cut only ~2%. This is broadly consistent with the market's own crowd price of 79% for 'no change', suggesting the market is reasonably efficient and a hold is the modal outcome, though there is meaningful tail risk of a hike given some recent inflationary pressure narratives found in search results.
results.key_findings: ["DeFiRate (prediction market aggregator, data ~Oct 2-14 2026): Oct 28 FOMC meeting priced at 84% hold, 18% hike, ~2% cut","Some sources indicate the Fed had been on a hiking path through mid-2026 (e.g., a reported 25bp hike to 3.75-4% around Sept 2026), implying inflation concerns could still be live into October","Other sources described a cutting cycle through late 2025 with a hold since March 2026 at 3.50-3.75%, indicating some inconsistency/uncertainty in available data about the exact rate path","Resolution defaults to 'No change' bracket if no statement is issued by the next meeting, which is not expected to be an issue given the meeting is confirmed for Oct 27-28, 2026"]

xvenue.read: polyMoves = minutes where Polymarket's mid moved >= 3c; staleKalshi = of those, Kalshi's same-minute quote was still crossable after its 7.000000000000001% x p(1-p) taker fee (avgStaleEdgeC = cents of edge per share); kalshiSameMin/NextMin = Kalshi moved the same way that minute / the next; kalshiLeads = Kalshi moved first and Polymarket followed. A Kalshi lane is worth building only if staleRate x avgStaleEdgeC is meaningfully positive over many games. us* = the same for Polymarket US (taker 6.950000000000001% x p(1-p)); kUsCross = minutes where buying on one US-legal venue and selling on the other cleared both taker fees (the only fully legal arbitrage pair for a US operator).

usLane.read: Paper only: each event is a hypothetical taker fill on Polymarket US at the sampled quote (px, qty = shares shown at that price; one event per game minute, on the leg the US instrument quotes). tradable = the subset with at least 50 shares shown (usd = dollars on the shown size, capped at 1000 shares) in a minute where global Polymarket's mid moved >= 3c and the US quote was still crossable after the 6.950000000000001% x p(1-p) taker fee (edgeC = cents of edge at entry). marks.* = cents per share after the entry fee, marked at global Polymarket's mid 1/5/15/60 minutes later and at the end of the game (final), and at settlement (0/1). Exit fees and the US spread are not charged. roiPct = avg mark pnl / avg entry price. noData = horizon passed with no sample. Decision rule (docs/PROFIT-AVENUES.md Part 2): after ~200 events, if m15 and settle are both positive after fees with a hit rate above 50% and the shown size is tradable, a Polymarket US lane is worth building; the real-money flip stays the operator's call.
